summaryEn: Bloomberg's "Risk Takers" profile of Elon Musk: from PayPal to founding SpaceX and building Tesla — the bets, the near-bankruptcies and the vision behind them.
summaryZh: 彭博《冒险者》对埃隆·马斯克的专题报道：从 PayPal 到创办 SpaceX 和打造 Tesla——这些赌注、几近破产的经历，以及背后的愿景。

segments.textEn: Elon Musk is a lot like the kid in the comic book whose fantasies turn into reality. But not as a magician. He did it as an engineer.
segments.textZh: 埃隆·马斯克很像漫画里那个幻想成真的孩子。但不是以魔术师的身份。他是以工程师的身份做到的。

segments.textEn: An engineer is the closest thing to a magician that exists in the real world.
segments.textZh: 工程师是现实世界中最接近魔术师的存在。

segments.textEn: Musk's fantasies and the companies they've inspired are transforming the way we live.
segments.textZh: 马斯克的幻想，以及受这些幻想启发而创立的公司，正在改变我们的生活方式。

segments.textEn: Like this guy is changing the world.
segments.textZh: 就像，这个人正在改变世界。

segments.textEn: He founded his first company at age 23 and sold it a few years later for $300 million. He helped pave the way for online commerce with PayPal.
segments.textZh: 他在 23 岁时创办了自己的第一家公司，几年后以 3 亿美元将其出售。他通过 PayPal 帮助铺平了在线商业的道路。

segments.textEn: His goal was to transform the financial industry.
segments.textZh: 他的目标是改变金融业。

segments.textEn: He made solar energy affordable and jump started the electric car industry.
segments.textZh: 他让太阳能变得负担得起，并推动电动汽车行业起步。

segments.textEn: We show that you can make compelling electric cars that people really want to buy.
segments.textZh: 我们证明了，可以制造出真正吸引人、让人们确实想买的电动汽车。

segments.textEn: And he's beating NASA to outer space.
segments.textZh: 而且他正在抢在 NASA 前面进军外太空。

segments.textEn: Elon Musk goes a step further. Earth, not big enough with SpaceX. He literally wants to go to Mars
segments.textZh: 埃隆·马斯克更进一步。有了 SpaceX，地球还不够大。他真的想去火星

segments.textEn: and he's still only 40.
segments.textZh: 而他仍然只有 40 岁。

segments.textEn: I look to him with awe at the way in which he can see the future and make it manifest.
segments.textZh: 他洞见未来并使其成为现实的方式令我敬畏。

segments.textEn: His greatest asset is his ability to take this big, big dream and make other people believe that it's true.
segments.textZh: 他最大的资本，是能够把这个非常、非常宏大的梦想讲出来，并让其他人相信它是真的。

segments.textEn: There have been setbacks.
segments.textZh: 期间也有过挫折。

segments.textEn: We have maybe about a week's worth of cash in the bank or less.
segments.textZh: 我们的银行账户里可能只剩大约够维持 1 周的现金，甚至更少。

segments.textEn: He saved the company in its darkest hour.
segments.textZh: 他在公司最黑暗的时刻挽救了它。

segments.textEn: And yes, he's controversial.
segments.textZh: 没错，他也颇具争议。

segments.textEn: This is just the religion of electric vehicles. And like Jonestown, that religion will come to an end.
segments.textZh: 这不过是电动汽车的宗教。而且就像琼斯镇一样，这个宗教终将走到尽头。

segments.textEn: Still, despite his critics, Musk has never been bashful about his own achievements.
segments.textZh: 不过，尽管有这些批评者，马斯克从不羞于谈论自己的成就。

segments.textEn: You know, Prius is a gas guzzling hog by comparison with this car.
segments.textZh: 你知道，相比这辆车，Prius 简直是一头狂喝汽油的猪。

segments.textEn: Yes, he's a media darling.
segments.textZh: 是的，他是媒体宠儿。

segments.textEn: On a scale of 1 to 10, how sexy am I going to be if I buy this car? I mean 11.
segments.textZh: 按 1 到 10 分来算，如果我买了这辆车，我会变得多性感？我的意思是，11 分。

segments.textEn: Here he is in the movie Iron Man. He was even the model for the movie's hero.
segments.textZh: 这是他在电影《钢铁侠》中的镜头。他甚至还是影片主人公的原型。

segments.textEn: Yeah, good idea for an electric jet.
segments.textZh: 对，电动喷气式飞机是个好主意。

segments.textEn: You do, then we'll make it work.
segments.textZh: 你来做，然后我们会让它运转起来。

segments.textEn: Go get it, Bob.
segments.textZh: 去把它弄来，鲍勃。

segments.textEn: You can bleep.
segments.textZh: 你可以消音。

segments.textEn: When I was a little kid, I was really scared of the dark.
segments.textZh: 我小时候真的很怕黑。

segments.textEn: But then I sort of came to understand, okay, well, dark just means really the absence of photons in the visible wavelength, 400 to 700 nanometers.
segments.textZh: 但后来我渐渐明白，好吧，黑暗其实只是意味着可见光波段中缺少光子，也就是 400 到 700 纳米。

segments.textEn: Elon's mother, May Musk.
segments.textZh: 埃隆的母亲，梅·马斯克。

segments.textEn: And Elon said, darkness is merely the absence of light.
segments.textZh: 然后埃隆说，黑暗只不过是光的缺失。

segments.textEn: Then I thought, well, it's really silly to be afraid of a lack of photons. Then I wasn't afraid of the dark anymore after that.
segments.textZh: 然后我想，嗯，害怕缺少光子实在很傻。从那以后，我就再也不怕黑了。

segments.textEn: Once one of the kids said to him, look at the moon. It's a billion miles away. And he said, well, no, it's actually under 250,000 miles away. And they said, oh, Elon, Elon Musk
segments.textZh: 有一次，一个孩子对他说，看月亮。它在 10 亿英里之外。他说，嗯，不，实际上它离这里不到 250,000 英里。然后他们说，哦，埃隆，埃隆·马斯克

segments.textEn: grew up in South Africa, the eldest of three children. His father was an engineer, his mother a model and nutritionist. Elon got off to a fast start and began school a year early.
segments.textZh: 在南非长大，是 3 个孩子中的老大。他的父亲是工程师，母亲是模特和营养师。埃隆起步很早，提前 1 年开始上学。

segments.textEn: He was the youngest. He made about two days and the shortest. And then he was this brilliant boy, and so people didn't really like him.
segments.textZh: 他是最小的。他大约过了 2 天，而且是最矮的。然后他又是个聪明绝顶的男孩，所以人们不太喜欢他。

segments.textEn: So I was this little bookwormy kid and probably a bit of a smart aleck. So this is a recipe for disaster.
segments.textZh: 所以我就是个小书呆子，可能还有点自作聪明。所以这就是一场灾难的配方。

segments.textEn: Not that he told me much about it, but he was picked on quite a bit.
segments.textZh: 虽然他没有跟我多说，但他确实经常受欺负。

segments.textEn: So I just, like, read a lot of books and tried to stay out of people's way during school.
segments.textZh: 所以我就，像是，读很多书，在学校期间尽量避开别人。

segments.textEn: And so his social life was much less than my other two kids. And that's a typical nerd.
segments.textZh: 所以他的社交生活比我另外 2 个孩子少得多。这就是典型的书呆子。

segments.textEn: I read all the comics I could buy or that they'd let me read at the bookstore before chasing me away. I read everything I could get my hands on from when I woke up to when I went to sleep. At one point, I really ran out of books and started reading the encyclopedia.
segments.textZh: 我读完了所有我买得起的漫画，或者书店在赶我走之前允许我看的漫画。从醒来到睡觉，我会阅读任何能拿到手的东西。有一阵子，我真的没书可读了，就开始读百科全书。

segments.textEn: And he has a photographic memory, so he could remember everything. Anytime I had a question, my daughter Tosca would say, call genius boy.
segments.textZh: 而且他有过目不忘的记忆力，所以他什么都能记住。每当我有问题时，我女儿托斯卡都会说，打电话给天才男孩。

segments.textEn: His brother, Kimball Musk.
segments.textZh: 他的弟弟，金巴尔·马斯克。

segments.textEn: When Elon was 10 years old, he got tested by IBM and he was found to have one of the highest aptitudes they'd ever seen for computer programming.
segments.textZh: 埃隆 10 岁时接受了 IBM 的测试，结果发现，他在计算机编程方面的天赋是他们见过的最高水平之一。

segments.textEn: I tried taking some computer classes, but I was way ahead of the teacher, so it didn't really help. So I started programming the space game called Blastar.
segments.textZh: 我试着上过一些计算机课程，但我远远领先于老师，所以并没有什么帮助。于是我开始编写一款名为 Blastar 的太空游戏。

segments.textEn: Musk, already thinking like an entrepreneur, figured out how to sell his game.
segments.textZh: 马斯克那时已经像企业家一样思考，并想出了如何出售自己的游戏。

segments.textEn: I don't think they realized. I was 12.
segments.textZh: 我觉得他们没有意识到。我当时 12 岁。

segments.textEn: We decided we were going to open an arcade out near our high school. We were big into video games. We figured that it was going to be a huge hit. We got a lease on a building. We got the arcade provider to deliver the equipment, and the only thing we needed to do by the end of it was get the city to approve what we were doing.
segments.textZh: 我们决定要在高中附近开一家游戏厅。我们非常痴迷电子游戏。我们认为它一定会大获成功。我们租下了一栋楼，让游戏机供应商送来了设备，到最后我们唯一需要做的，就是让市政府批准我们正在做的事。

segments.textEn: But an adult had to apply for a city permit, and they hadn't told their parents what they were up to.
segments.textZh: 但必须由成年人申请市政许可，而他们还没把自己在做什么告诉父母。

segments.textEn: But of course, they told us we were not going to be opening up an arcade.
segments.textZh: 但当然，他们告诉我们，我们不能开游戏厅。

segments.textEn: Really, the most amazing thing about his childhood is his escape from South Africa.
segments.textZh: 说真的，他童年时代最令人惊叹的事情，是他逃离南非。

segments.textEn: I remember thinking and saying that America is where great things are possible, more than any other country in the world. It's a little cliche, but it's true. America is the land of opportunity.
segments.textZh: 我记得自己曾想过，也曾说过，与世界上任何其他国家相比，美国是更有可能成就伟大事业的地方。这话有点老套，但确实如此。美国是机会之地。

segments.textEn: Elon came and told me that he wants to go to Canada. He really wanted to go to the United States. As A Canadian born, I could get my citizenship back and then I could pass it on to my children.
segments.textZh: 埃隆过来告诉我，他想去加拿大。他真正想去的是美国。由于我出生在加拿大，我可以恢复自己的公民身份，然后把它传给我的孩子。

segments.textEn: Musk wanted to avoid serving in South Africa's army and as he put it, suppressing black people.
segments.textZh: 马斯克想避免在南非军队服役，以及用他的话说，压迫黑人。

segments.textEn: Growing up in apartheid South Africa was pretty surreal. We didn't support that government, we didn't believe in it. And so the idea of actually going to the military service was really out of the question.
segments.textZh: 在实行种族隔离的南非长大，感觉相当超现实。我们不支持那个政府，也不认同它。所以，真正去服兵役这个想法完全不在考虑之列。

segments.textEn: I told my parents I was going to Canada and they tried to convince me not to leave.
segments.textZh: 我告诉父母我要去加拿大，他们试图说服我不要离开。

segments.textEn: And off he flew. And I thought, wow, he's so independent. Of course, as soon as he lands, he calls me and he says, what do I do now?
segments.textZh: 然后他就飞走了。我心想，哇，他真独立。当然，他一落地就给我打电话，说，我现在该怎么办？

segments.textEn: He arrived with little money and almost no prospects.
segments.textZh: 他抵达时身上没多少钱，也几乎没有任何前途可言。

segments.textEn: So I bought a bus ticket from Montreal to Vancouver and that allowed me to kind of see Canada, at least from the highway.
segments.textZh: 所以我买了一张从蒙特利尔到温哥华的长途汽车票，这让我算是看了看加拿大，至少是从公路上看。

segments.textEn: He worked at odd jobs across the country before settling at Queens College in Toronto.
segments.textZh: 他在全国各地打零工，之后就读于多伦多的皇后学院。

segments.textEn: In fact, when I went to college, I rarely went to class. I just read the textbook and then show up for exams. The big appeal at university was being able to date girls my own age. Actually met my first wife there.
segments.textZh: 事实上，我上大学时很少去上课。我只是读课本，然后到考试时露面。大学最吸引人的地方，是可以和与我同龄的女孩约会。实际上，我在那里遇到了我的第一任妻子。

segments.textEn: Justine Wilson was an English major from Southern Ontario. They put off marriage for 10 years. Musk still dreamed of reaching America and changing the world.
segments.textZh: 贾斯汀·威尔逊是来自安大略省南部的英语专业学生。他们把结婚推迟了 10 年。马斯克依然梦想着抵达美国并改变世界。

segments.textEn: I really wanted to just kind of go where the really exciting breakthroughs were occurring.
segments.textZh: 我真的只想去那些真正激动人心的突破正在发生的地方。

segments.textEn: He got an engineering and business degree from the University of Pennsylvania and a scholarship to go to Stanford University. Silicon Valley was the place to be.
segments.textZh: 他获得了宾夕法尼亚大学的工程和商科学位，以及前往斯坦福大学深造的奖学金。硅谷是非去不可的地方。

segments.textEn: Elon had this ability to look at the world, go, this is a real problem that's going to happen in 20 years.
segments.textZh: 埃隆有这种能力，他审视世界，然后说，这是一个将在 20 年后真正出现的问题。

segments.textEn: The Internet, sustainable energy and extending life beyond Earth, making life multi planetary now. I didn't actually expect to ever have the opportunity to be involved in space. So this is not from the standpoint of these are the things I'm going to do. It's from the standpoint of in the absolute. These are the things that I think will most affect the future of humanity.
segments.textZh: 互联网、可持续能源，以及把生命延伸到地球以外，现在就是让生命成为多行星物种。其实我从没想过自己会有机会参与太空事业。所以，这并不是站在“这些就是我要做的事”的角度。而是从绝对意义上说，这些是我认为将对人类未来产生最大影响的事情。

segments.textEn: Max Chavkin writes for Inc. Magazine and profiled Musk in 2007 and again in 2010. After spending several weeks with his subject,
segments.textZh: 马克斯·查夫金为《Inc.》杂志撰稿，并分别于 2007 年和 2010 年为马斯克撰写了人物专题。在与采访对象相处数周后，

segments.textEn: he looked around and he saw that the world changing stuff was not happening at Stanford.
segments.textZh: 他环顾四周，发现那些改变世界的事情并没有发生在斯坦福。

segments.textEn: I didn't even go to class. I called the chair of the department and said, I'd like to try selling this Internet company. It probably won't succeed. And so when it fails, I want to make sure that I can still come back.
segments.textZh: 我甚至没有去上课。我给系主任打电话说，我想试着卖掉这家互联网公司。它很可能不会成功。所以等它失败时，我想确保自己仍然可以回来。

segments.textEn: My kids do funny things and I'm never too concerned about them because, you know, if Elon wanted to drop out of college, he could always go back.
segments.textZh: 我的孩子们会做些有趣的事，而我从来不会太担心他们，因为，你知道，如果埃隆想从大学退学，他随时可以回去。

segments.textEn: My brother was in Canada at the time, and I said, look, I think we should try to create an Internet company. So he came down and joined me.
segments.textZh: 我的兄弟当时在加拿大，我说，听着，我觉得我们应该试着创办一家互联网公司。于是他南下加入了我。

segments.textEn: He had $2,000, no friends, barely enough money for an apartment. I think he told me he was showering at the gym because they didn't have a show where he was living.
segments.textZh: 他有 2,000 美元，没有朋友，钱勉强够租一套公寓。我记得他告诉我，他会去健身房洗澡，因为他住的地方没有一场演出。

segments.textEn: And we spent six months sleeping in the office.
segments.textZh: 我们在办公室里睡了 6 个月。

segments.textEn: We just got some. A few tons that there were couches during the day and then turned into beds at night.
segments.textZh: 我们就弄来了一些。几吨东西，白天是沙发，晚上再变成床。

segments.textEn: Steve Jurgensen is a venture capitalist in Silicon Valley.
segments.textZh: 史蒂夫·尤尔根森是硅谷的一名风险投资家。

segments.textEn: I first met Elon N. Kimble Musk, his brother, back in the mid-90s when they first set foot in California. I think they'd been here for about a week, and they were pitching a new company called Zip2. Silicon Valley in the mid-90s and late-90s was a gold rush. People were flocking to the region to find riches to make it in the Internet business.
segments.textZh: 我第一次见到埃隆·N·金布尔·马斯克和他的弟弟，是在 90 年代中期，当时他们刚刚踏上加利福尼亚的土地。我想他们来这里大约 1 周了，当时正在推介一家名为 Zip2 的新公司。90 年代中期和 90 年代末期的硅谷是一场淘金热。人们蜂拥到这个地区寻找财富，想在互联网行业闯出名堂。

segments.textEn: Elon was more the business mastermind. I was more the sales guy.
segments.textZh: 埃隆更像是商业策划高手。我更像是销售人员。

segments.textEn: I still had my core programming skills, so I was able to write the software needed for the first company.
segments.textZh: 我仍然具备自己的核心编程技能，所以能够编写第一家公司所需的软件。

segments.textEn: Now, when Elon was starting zip two, keep in mind, the Internet was just a couple of years old. Most local businesses were not on the Internet. And the way you found a local business was you opened up the yellow pages.
segments.textZh: 现在，要记住，埃隆创办 zip two 时，互联网才诞生几年。大多数本地商家都不在互联网上。而寻找本地商家的方式，就是翻开黄页。

segments.textEn: It was 1995 when Musk came up with an idea to bring newspapers into the digital age. Elon took a CD rom, yellow pages, some mapping software, wrote a little code, and put it all together to create the first online city listings.
segments.textZh: 1995 年，马斯克想出了一个让报纸进入数字时代的主意。埃隆拿来一张 CD rom、黄页和一些地图软件，写了少量代码，把它们整合在一起，创建了第一份在线城市名录。

segments.textEn: The thought was that media companies, like the newspapers, are going to need help coming online and building lots of functionality into their websites.
segments.textZh: 当时的想法是，报纸之类的媒体公司将需要帮助，以便上线，并在网站中构建大量功能。

segments.textEn: So Zip2 was sort of like an early version of what we have with Google Maps.
segments.textZh: 所以 Zip2 有点像我们现在所拥有的 Google 地图的早期版本。

segments.textEn: We had someone literally throw a yellow pages book at us and tell us, do you think you'll ever replace this? And we thought the guy was crazy because not only were we going to replace this, but that's not where it ended. It would keep going from there.
segments.textZh: 真的有人把一本黄页扔向我们，并对我们说，你们觉得自己有朝一日能取代这个吗？我们觉得那个人疯了，因为我们不仅会取代它，而且事情不会到此为止。还会从那里继续发展下去。

segments.textEn: It wasn't long before media companies across the country were signing up.
segments.textZh: 没过多久，全国各地的媒体公司都纷纷签约。

segments.textEn: And so we were able to get as investors and customers, the New York Times company, Hearst, knightritter, and a number of other companies.
segments.textZh: 于是，我们得以让纽约时报公司、赫斯特、奈特里特以及其他多家公司成为我们的投资者和客户。

segments.textEn: In 1999, the Alta Vista division of Compaq bought Zip2 for $307 million in cash and 34 million in stock options. Elon was 28 years old.
segments.textZh: 1999 年，康柏旗下的 Alta Vista 部门以 3.07 亿美元现金和价值 3,400 万美元的股票期权收购了 Zip2。埃隆当时 28 岁。

segments.textEn: I thought, that's crazy. Why would somebody pay such a huge amount of money for this little company that we have? It actually, obviously Turned out very well for them financially, so they knew a lot more about it than I did.
segments.textZh: 我当时想，这太疯狂了。为什么会有人为我们这家小公司支付如此巨额的资金？实际上，显然，这后来为他们带来了非常可观的财务回报，所以他们对此的了解远比我多。

segments.textEn: When the kids sold two, it was the most exciting day. We couldn't believe it, because you don't know in the Internet world if you're going to, you know, make a million or die tomorrow.
segments.textZh: 孩子们卖掉 2 的那天，是最令人兴奋的一天。我们简直不敢相信，因为在互联网世界里，你不知道自己会，你知道，赚到 100 万，还是明天就死掉。

segments.textEn: In 1999, Elon Musk sold his first company in the brave new world of silicon valley. He was a millionaire at the age of 28.
segments.textZh: 1999 年，埃隆·马斯克在硅谷这个勇敢的新世界里卖掉了自己的第一家公司。他在 28 岁时成为了百万富翁。

segments.textEn: Software was acquired by Compaq for a little over $300 million. And I made, I think, about 21 or $22 million as a result of that, which was a phenomenal amount of money for me.
segments.textZh: 软件被康柏以略高于 3 亿美元的价格收购。而我因此赚了，我想，大约 2,100 万或 2,200 万美元，对我来说这是一笔惊人的巨款。

segments.textEn: It was obviously a financial windfall. It was super fun to go out and buy some cool toys.
segments.textZh: 这显然是一笔意外之财。出去买些很酷的玩具，特别有趣。

segments.textEn: There is John, and the fastest car in the world.
segments.textZh: 那是约翰，还有世界上最快的汽车。

He comes from a family that really enjoys racing and vehicles, and he got one of the highest performance cars money could buy at the time. segments.textZh: 他最先做的事情之一，就是出去买一辆大型跑车。他的家人非常喜欢赛车和车辆，他买下了当时金钱所能买到的最高性能汽车之一。那是一辆迈凯伦 F1，之后他就在湾区享受驾驶它的乐趣，可以说，他开车时经历了许多冒险，也犯下了错误动作。

segments.textEn: While I'm sure it felt wonderful to have all this money and to have people recognizing success, I think he was also frustrated that this company hadn't become as great as he wanted it to be. segments.textZh: 虽然我相信，拥有这么多钱、得到人们对成功的认可，感觉一定很棒，但我认为他也感到沮丧，因为这家公司没有变得像他希望的那样伟大。它没有改变世界。它只是略微改变了报业历史的进程，我认为从他的角度来看，这算是一项微不足道的成就。

segments.textEn: I certainly had the choice at that point of retiring and buying an island somewhere and sipping mai tais, but that was not of interest to me at all.

segments.textEn: He was very rich. I mean, just more money than most people could dream. And he took almost no time in between that sale and starting the company that became paypal.
segments.textZh: 他非常富有。我的意思是，他拥有的钱比大多数人梦想的还多。而在那次出售与创办后来成为 PayPal 的公司之间，他几乎没有休息。

segments.textEn: The goal in doing my second Internet company was to. To create something that would have a profound effect. It seems like something that should lend itself to innovation.
segments.textZh: 我创办第2家互联网公司的目标是。是创造一种能够产生深远影响的东西。在我看来，金融行业在互联网上并没有出现很多创新。而钱其实只是数据库中的一条记录。所以它所需的带宽很低。它似乎很适合进行创新。

segments.textEn: Musk's new company created something we take for granted today. It changed forever the way the world buys things, the way money goes from one person to another.
segments.textZh: 马斯克的新公司创造了某种如今被我们视为理所当然的东西。它永远改变了全世界购买物品的方式，改变了资金从一个人转到另一个人的方式。

segments.textEn: At the time, transactions were Very slow. People would have to mail checks to each other. So it could take weeks just to complete a single transaction.

segments.textEn: And they were really competing against each other. And the real enemy at the end of the day was ebay.

segments.textEn: We combined our efforts in order to compete effectively against ebay's built in system.
segments.textZh: 为了有效对抗 eBay 的内置系统，我们合并了双方的力量。

segments.textZh: 他们将新公司命名为 PayPal。

segments.textEn: When he looked at PayPal, his goal was not to create a place you could do person to person payments. His goal was to transform the financial industry.
segments.textZh: 当他看待 PayPal 时，他的目标并不是创建一个可供人们进行个人对个人付款的平台。他的目标是改造金融业。

segments.textEn: We're able to become the leading payment system in the world. And then eBay finally threw in the towel and acquired PayPal.
segments.textZh: 我们得以成为世界领先的支付系统。然后 eBay 终于认输，收购了 PayPal。

segments.textEn: In early 2002, Musk and his partners sold PayPal for 1.5 billion. Musk, still only 30, walked away from the deal with roughly $180 million.
segments.textZh: 2002年初，马斯克及其合伙人以15亿出售了 PayPal。当时仍只有30岁的马斯克从这笔交易中获得了约1.8亿美元。

segments.textEn: I could have bought probably a chain of islands, but again, that was obviously not of interest to me.

segments.textZh: 那么接下来呢？最后的疆域，太空。

segments.textEn: It's just a much more exciting, inspiring future if we're out there exploring the stars as opposed to a future where we are forever confined to Earth.
segments.textZh: 如果我们能在那里探索群星，未来就会更加激动人心、鼓舞人心，而不是永远被困在地球上的那种未来。

segments.textEn: He had what might seem a completely absurd notion that he just assumed he could pull off.

segments.textEn: I was thinking, well, I wonder when we're going to Mars, when is NASA going to go to Mars? And I went to the NASA website and there was no plan to go to Mars and no plan to reach really even take the next step in space exploration.
segments.textZh: 我当时在想，嗯，我们什么时候去火星，NASA 什么时候会去火星？然后我访问了 NASA 的网站，上面没有前往火星的计划，也没有真正达到、甚至迈出太空探索下一步的计划。

segments.textEn: This is Elon saying he wants to go and enable human civilization to leave the planet Earth. It's about as big a vision as you could possibly imagine. And that's going to require funds. And he has enough funds to go do it, so he's going to go do it.
segments.textZh: 这是埃隆在说，他想要促成人类文明离开地球。这几乎是你所能想象到的最宏大的愿景。而这需要资金。他有足够的资金去做，所以他就要去做。

segments.textEn: He had the outrageous idea that a private enterprise could actually re energize space travel. In June 2002, he founded Space Exploration Technologies, or SpaceX.

segments.textEn: And I came to the conclusion that the thing that was really holding us back from making much more progress is space. It was really that rockets had not evolved since the 60s.
segments.textZh: 而我得出的结论是，真正阻碍我们取得更大进展的是太空。其实是火箭从60年代起就没有进化过。

segments.textEn: What SpaceX has been very successful at is taking basically off the shelf technology stuff that was developed by NASA 50 years ago and streamlining it. segments.textZh: SpaceX 做得非常成功的一点，是采用基本上可以直接取用的技术，也就是 NASA 在50年前开发的东西，并对其进行精简。因此从这个意义上说，他有点像太空领域的亨利·福特，因为亨利·福特并没有发明汽车，他只是弄清楚了如何让汽车具备商业可行性。

segments.textEn: But Musk was more than just an entrepreneur.
segments.textZh: 但马斯克不只是一名企业家。

segments.textZh: 埃隆没有受过航空工程师的专业训练，然而他，他却有能力在那个特定领域取得巨大成功。

segments.textEn: He's deeply involved with product architecture, design and engineering, More so with SpaceX, but with all of his companies.
segments.textZh: 他深度参与产品架构、设计和工程，在 SpaceX 尤其如此，但他所有的公司都是这样。

segments.textZh: 如果你问埃隆他是怎样自学火箭科学的，他会非常严肃地看着你，然后非常轻声地说，我读了很多书。

And who had started a few companies of their own.

And they say okay, and it works almost perfectly.
segments.textZh: 他有这么一个想法：我们要做太阳能电池板领域的戴尔电脑。我们要让任何人在自家屋顶安装太阳能电池板都变得非常、非常、非常容易。然后他基本上把这个想法交给表亲，说，如果你们想创办这家公司，我会给你们提供资金，它会是你们的公司，但我会担任董事长。他们答应了，而事情几乎完美地奏效了。

segments.textZh: 他们想明白的是，如果你在面向家庭业主的太阳能电池安装领域，把大约100件事情都改进10%，就能大幅整合这个目前由一大批夫妻店组成的行业。所以 SolarCities 的做法是，他们说，不如不用付首付吧，你想要太阳能电池，我们直接给你装上。

segments.textZh: 你一分钱都不用付。

segments.textZh: 没有。

segments.textEn: When we first saw Tesla, it had a good explanation for how they get to market without having to spend exorbitant amount of money. How they would create a brand and a object of desire in consumers. And each part of the story clicked together.
segments.textZh: 我们第一次看到Tesla时，它很好地解释了他们如何在不必花费高得离谱的资金的情况下进入市场。他们将如何打造一个品牌，并在消费者心中创造一个渴望拥有的对象。这个故事的每一部分都衔接在了一起。

segments.textEn: Alan Onsman is a reporter for Bloomberg News.
segments.textZh: 艾伦·昂斯曼是彭博新闻社的记者。

segments.textEn: He talked about Silicon Valley smarts. Being able to show Detroit how to do something that Detroit didn't think was possible.
segments.textZh: 他谈到了硅谷的智慧。能够向底特律展示如何做到一件底特律认为不可能的事。

segments.textEn: Its batteries, its drive electronics, its electric motors, those are skills that are present in Silicon Valley and not present in Detroit.
segments.textZh: 它的电池、驱动电子设备、电动机，这些都是硅谷具备而底特律不具备的技能。

segments.textEn: Tesla's revolutionary technology started with a computer battery as the power source for an automobile.
segments.textZh: Tesla的革命性技术始于用电脑电池作为汽车的动力来源。

segments.textEn: For the first time, it was possible to drive over 200 miles and have performance that was directly comparable, competitive with what a gasoline car could do. And Tesla was the first company to take those principles and put that into practice and try it.
segments.textZh: 第一次，行驶超过200英里成为可能，而且其性能可以与汽油车所能做到的直接相比、形成竞争。Tesla是第一家采用这些原理、将其付诸实践并进行尝试的公司。

segments.textEn: An electric car, if designed right, is all about torque. It means that at any speed you're driving, if you step on it, it's there instantly. So you can step on it and this hauls ass.
segments.textZh: 电动汽车如果设计得当，关键全在于扭矩。这意味着，无论你以什么速度行驶，只要踩下去，动力就会立即到来。所以你可以踩下去，然后这车就猛冲出去。

segments.textEn: The Governator himself showed up for Tesla's 2006 coming out party.
segments.textZh: 州长侠本人出席了Tesla在2006年的亮相活动。

segments.textEn: A test drove this one.
segments.textZh: A试驾了这辆。

segments.textEn: It's hard.
segments.textZh: 这很难。

segments.textEn: He bought one. So did Leo DiCaprio and George Clooney. But could Musk sell regular consumers on the idea? The electric car still had an image problem.
segments.textZh: 他买了一辆。莱昂纳多·迪卡普里奥和乔治·克鲁尼也买了。但马斯克能让普通消费者接受这个想法吗？电动汽车仍然存在形象问题。

segments.textEn: At that time, there was very little activity in the auto industry in electric vehicles. We were in the age of the large suv. So it was a little unusual to hear about this company in California that was planning to come to market with a high end all electric sports car.
segments.textZh: 当时，汽车行业在电动汽车方面几乎没有什么动静。我们正处于大型SUV的时代。所以，听说加利福尼亚州这家公司计划向市场推出一款高端纯电动跑车，多少有点不同寻常。

segments.textEn: J.B. straubel, Tesla's chief technology officer, was the main designer of the electric powertrain.
segments.textZh: Tesla首席技术官J.B. 施特劳贝尔是电动动力总成的主要设计者。

segments.textEn: We were very passionate about trying to make sure that this car was going to just throw down the gauntlet on what the technology could do and really prove to the world that electric vehicles could be incredibly fast and could have incredibly long range. There was kind of a sense of adventure, you know, doing these things for the first time and doing it in a really scrappy way. We did some of the very first battery packs in my garage in Menlo park before we actually were able to rent a real office.
segments.textZh: 我们非常热衷于努力确保这辆车会在技术能力方面直接发起挑战，并真正向全世界证明，电动汽车可以快得惊人，也可以拥有长得惊人的续航里程。这里面有一种冒险感，你知道，第一次做这些事情，而且用一种真正因陋就简的方式去做。在我们真正租得起一间像样的办公室之前，我们在我位于门洛帕克的车库里制作了最早的一批电池组。

segments.textEn: The big issue for Tesla, as with all electric cars, has been the batteries, their cost, and how long they last. Eric Noble is president of Car Lab, an Orange, California consulting firm that evaluates new cars and trucks.
segments.textZh: 对于Tesla而言，就像所有电动汽车一样，最大的问题一直是电池、它们的成本以及它们能用多久。埃里克·诺布尔是Car Lab的总裁，这是一家位于加利福尼亚州奥兰治、评估新型轿车和卡车的咨询公司。

segments.textEn: American consumers are very ready for battery electric vehicles. Unfortunately, battery electric vehicles aren't ready for American consumers.
segments.textZh: 美国消费者已经非常愿意接受纯电动汽车。不幸的是，纯电动汽车还没有准备好迎接美国消费者。

segments.textEn: The first results at Tesla seemed to support this gloomy forecast.
segments.textZh: Tesla 最初的结果似乎印证了这一悲观预测。

segments.textEn: Tesla, when we first started out, the thought was simple and really, obviously in retrospect, quite naive, which was to make use of a Lotus chassis, some technology that we develop ourselves, but we system technology that would license from AC propulsion, put that together and create an electric sports car that would be compelling. So let's see, where did that fall apart?
segments.textZh: Tesla，最初起步时，我们的想法很简单，现在回想起来，显然也相当幼稚，那就是利用莲花汽车的底盘，加上一些我们自行开发的技术，但我们会从 AC Propulsion 获得系统技术许可，把这些结合起来，打造一款有吸引力的电动跑车。那么看看，问题是从哪里开始的？

segments.textEn: The car that Musk's team told him could be made for $65,000 would actually cost 140,000 just for raw materials.
segments.textZh: 马斯克的团队告诉他，这款车可以用65,000美元造出来，但实际上仅原材料就要花费140,000美元。

segments.textEn: When we found out that the costs were a lot higher than expected, it was a, a very frustrating time for us.
segments.textZh: 当我们发现成本远高于预期时，那对我们来说是一段、一段非常令人沮丧的时期。

segments.textEn: As the problems mounted, Musk faced a do or die decision at Tesla. Would he let the company collapse or invest his nest egg, the 160 million dollar fortune he'd made from the sale of PayPal. The bet of a lifetime.
segments.textZh: 随着问题不断增多，马斯克在 Tesla 面临一个生死攸关的决定。他会任由公司垮掉，还是投入自己的积蓄，也就是他出售 PayPal 所赚得的1.6亿美元财富。这是一生中最大的一场豪赌。

segments.textEn: By 2007, Tesla was running out of money fast. No one wanted to step up to save the unproven automobile startup. Elon had to take the leap alone.
segments.textZh: 到2007年，Tesla 的资金正迅速耗尽。没有人愿意站出来拯救这家未经验证的汽车初创公司。埃隆只能独自冒险一搏。

segments.textEn: We have to make some pretty dramatic changes, essentially recapitalize the business and invest about twice what we'd originally expected. What we really expected is the outer limit.
segments.textZh: 我们必须做出一些相当重大的改变，实质上是对公司进行资本重组，并投入大约相当于最初预期2倍的资金。我们真正预期的是上限。

segments.textEn: And Elon was looking at this and saying, the dream is still there, but oh my gosh, what have I got? I've got to get this under control.
segments.textZh: 埃隆看着这一切，说，梦想依然还在，但我的天啊，我现在面对的是什么？我必须控制住局面。

segments.textEn: Basically, Tesla got to this point where they only had enough money in the bank for a couple of months and there's nobody around who are willing to put more money in.
segments.textZh: 基本上，Tesla 到了这样一个地步：银行里的钱只够维持几个月，而且周围没有任何人愿意再投入更多资金。

segments.textEn: I take all of my reserve capital and invest it into Tesla, which was very scary because, you know, it would obviously be quite sad to have the fruits of my labor with Zip2 and PayPal not amount to anything. But there was no question that I would do that in my own mind because Tesla was too important. To let die. I'm available 247 to help solve issues. Call me 3am on a Sunday morning. I don't care.
segments.textZh: 我拿出全部储备资金投入 Tesla，这非常吓人，因为，你知道，如果我在 Zip2 和 PayPal 上的劳动成果最终化为乌有，显然会非常令人难过。但在我自己心里，我毫无疑问会这么做，因为 Tesla 太重要了。不能任其死去。我全天247都可以帮忙解决问题。星期天凌晨3点给我打电话。我不在乎。

segments.textEn: We had to go in and make some really hard decisions on personnel changes. And Elon really had to dedicate his time to the company.
segments.textZh: 我们不得不介入，并在人事变动方面做出一些非常艰难的决定。埃隆也确实必须把自己的时间投入公司。

segments.textEn: I want names named. So if someone's always on the hot seat and is always the root cause for problems, they will not be part of this organization. Long term income. It's not okay to be unhappy and part of this company. If somebody can't get happy, get divorced.
segments.textZh: 我要点出名字。所以，如果某个人总是如坐针毡，而且始终是问题的根源，他们就不会是这个组织的一员。长期收入。不开心却还留在这家公司是不行的。如果有人无法开心起来，那就离婚。

segments.textEn: Musk and his board replaced Martin Everhard, one of their co founders who had been running Tesla.
segments.textZh: 马斯克及其董事会撤换了马丁·埃弗哈德，他是一直负责运营 Tesla 的联合创始人之一。

segments.textEn: And I think we kind of really exceeded the level that Everhart could handle. And that became apparent in 2007.
segments.textZh: 我认为，我们确实有些超出了埃弗哈特所能应付的程度。而这一点在2007年变得很明显。

segments.textEn: We either were going to have to shut the company down or Elon Musk have to take over as CEO.
segments.textZh: 我们要么必须关闭公司，要么埃隆·马斯克必须接任首席执行官。

segments.textEn: It was actually a process of building a company as well as building a car. You know, a lot of people that fit in very well with the company when it was extremely small, you know, didn't end up, you know, fitting in as well when it was larger.
segments.textZh: 实际上，这是一个既要打造公司、又要制造汽车的过程。你知道，很多在公司规模极小时非常适合公司的人，你知道，最后在公司规模扩大后，你知道，就没那么适合了。

segments.textEn: Eberhard didn't go quietly. He sued Elon for libel, slander and breach of contract.
segments.textZh: 埃伯哈德并未悄然离开。他以书面诽谤、口头诽谤和违约为由起诉了埃隆。

segments.textEn: I believe that I was scapegoated to
segments.textZh: 我认为，我被当成了替罪羊，来

segments.textEn: take the blame for the programs that
segments.textZh: 为那些项目承担责任，而那些

segments.textEn: were not run well.
segments.textZh: 运营得不好。

segments.textEn: Musk resolved the dispute through mediation, but his company was in serious financial trouble. In September 2007, Musk flew to Germany with a scheme to raise extra cash by forging an alliance with Daimler Mercedes.
segments.textZh: 马斯克通过调解解决了争端，但他的公司陷入了严重的财务困境。2007年9月，马斯克飞往德国，计划通过与戴姆勒-梅赛德斯结盟来筹集额外资金。

segments.textEn: Daimler is the company that invented the internal combustion engine car, the maker of Mercedes Smart. And their endorsement carries a great deal of weight. So that, that was just a very important moment.
segments.textZh: 戴姆勒是发明内燃机汽车的公司，也是梅赛德斯 Smart 的制造商。他们的认可分量极重。所以，那、那确实是一个非常重要的时刻。

segments.textEn: He had to convince the company that Tesla could supply battery packs for Daimler's cars. But his PowerPoint demo failed miserably.
segments.textZh: 他必须让这家公司相信，Tesla 能够为戴姆勒的汽车供应电池组。但他的 PowerPoint 演示彻底失败了。

segments.textEn: Really, the key thing with Daimler was to demonstrate hardware that worked.
segments.textZh: 实际上，与戴姆勒合作的关键是展示能够运行的硬件。

segments.textEn: You know, if they can't touch it, they can't drive it. It's not particularly real.
segments.textZh: 你知道，如果他们摸不到它，也开不了它。它就不算特别真实。

segments.textEn: To convince the Germans of the potential of the electric car, he asked his team to retrofit a Daimler Smart Car with Tesla's electric motor.
segments.textZh: 为了让德国人相信电动汽车的潜力，他要求团队为一辆戴姆勒 Smart 汽车改装 Tesla 的电动机。

segments.textEn: The challenge of converting a Smart Car to electric was doubly difficult because we couldn't find a Smart car.
segments.textZh: 将一辆 Smart 汽车改装成电动车的挑战难上加难，因为我们找不到 Smart 汽车。

segments.textEn: The Smart Car is not for sale in the United States. So we had to send somebody down to Mexico to buy a Smart car, bring, bring one to the US and then the Smart Car is really tiny, so we had to fit a motor and power electronics and charger and everything in The Smart Car.
segments.textZh: Smart汽车不在美国销售。所以我们不得不派人去墨西哥买一辆Smart汽车，带、带一辆到美国，然后Smart汽车真的很小，所以我们不得不把电机、电力电子设备、充电器和所有东西都装进Smart汽车里。

segments.textEn: The challenge was daunting. To replace the Smart Car's gas engine with a Tesla drivetrain and battery, fit it in a tiny space under the hood, and do it all in less than four weeks.
segments.textZh: 这项挑战令人望而生畏。要用Tesla的传动系统和电池替换Smart汽车的汽油发动机，将其装入引擎盖下方的狭小空间，并且在不到4周内完成这一切。

segments.textEn: We didn't have much time at all. We knew that from the beginning, and we kind of prepared for almost battle and, you know, set up war room in the shop.
segments.textZh: 我们根本没有多少时间。我们从一开始就知道这一点，于是有点像为战斗做准备，而且，你知道，在车间里设立了作战室。

segments.textEn: They worked around the clock, stealing naps on the factory floor right up to the deadline.
segments.textZh: 他们夜以继日地工作，就在工厂地板上抽空打盹，一直干到最后期限。

segments.textEn: The Daimler executives arrived and not at all convinced that it made any sense to work with an American car company, let alone a little tiny American car company in Silicon Valley.
segments.textZh: 戴姆勒的高管们来了，他们完全不相信与一家美国汽车公司合作有任何道理，更不用说是硅谷的一家小小的美国汽车公司了。

segments.textEn: The Daimler executive went for a test drive. When he came back, a breakthrough. A $70 million contract for Tesla to make electric Smart car batteries. This gave Musk the confidence to start building a competitively priced sedan. He called it the Model S. Taking his cue from the original Model T, he wanted a family car that was modern and sexy. So he hired the man who had designed the latest Aston Martin, James Bond's new ride in Casino Royale.
segments.textZh: 戴姆勒的高管去试驾了。他回来时，出现了突破。Tesla获得了一份价值7000万美元的合同，为Smart电动汽车制造电池。这让马斯克有信心开始制造一款价格具有竞争力的轿车。他称之为Model S。借鉴最初的Model T，他想要一辆既现代又性感的家用汽车。于是，他聘请了设计最新款阿斯顿·马丁的那个人；这款车正是詹姆斯·邦德在《皇家赌场》中的新座驾。

segments.textEn: Originally with Model S, we thought, well, let's have Henrik Fisker, who had a design studio do the styling. We paid him a pretty good sum of money to do that, curiously enough. The designs that he. He worked on, that he came up with for us were terrible.
segments.textZh: 最初做Model S时，我们想，嗯，就让拥有一家设计工作室的亨里克·菲斯克来负责造型设计吧。说来也奇怪，我们为此付给了他一笔相当可观的钱。他所做的设计。他为我们做出来的那些设计糟透了。

segments.textEn: And what he didn't tell us was that he was actually working on a competing car company.
segments.textZh: 而他没有告诉我们的是，他实际上正在筹办一家与我们竞争的汽车公司。

segments.textEn: Tesla officials claimed that perhaps Henrik had come in to learn what Tesla was doing, while all along he was planning to form his own company, do his own vehicle.
segments.textZh: Tesla的官员声称，亨里克来这里或许是为了了解Tesla在做什么，而他一直都在计划成立自己的公司，制造自己的汽车。

segments.textEn: We were pretty upset with him for basically taking what were, at the time, the original specifications for the Model S, and then going and shopping a business plan to create that same car.
segments.textZh: 我们对他相当恼火，因为他基本上拿走了当时Model S的原始规格，然后到处推销一份制造同一款汽车的商业计划。

segments.textEn: Tesla sued him. He sued Tesla, and there was all kinds of, you know, infighting.
segments.textZh: Tesla起诉了他。他也起诉了Tesla，而且出现了各种各样的，你知道，内部争斗。

segments.textEn: Henrik Fisker wouldn't grant Bloomberg an interview, but he told us that I believe there is enough space in the market for several new car companies that pursue a new type of electrified powertrain with different philosophies. In 2008, the court ruled in Fisker's favor. It was a minor setback for Musk, but the beginning of what would turn out to be the hardest year of his life.
segments.textZh: 亨里克·菲斯克不愿接受彭博社的采访，但他告诉我们：“我相信，市场有足够的空间容纳数家秉持不同理念、追求新型电气化动力系统的新汽车公司。”2008年，法院裁定菲斯克胜诉。对马斯克来说，这是一次小挫折，却也是后来被证明为他人生中最艰难一年之开端。

segments.textEn: It's always difficult to find the right partner in business or in one's personal life, and you don't always make the right choices.
segments.textZh: 无论在商业中找到合适的合作伙伴，还是在个人生活中找到合适的伴侣，都总是很困难，而且你并不总能作出正确的选择。

segments.textEn: In fact, Musk's personal life wasn't working out either. He had married Justine in 2000. They have five kids, all born within two years. Then the marriage fell apart. Justine felt that Musk's work always came first.
segments.textZh: 事实上，马斯克的个人生活也出了问题。他于2000年与贾丝廷结婚。他们有5个孩子，全都在2年内出生。后来这段婚姻破裂了。贾丝廷觉得马斯克总是把工作放在第一位。

segments.textEn: I had the sense of being relegated and sidelined and, you know, that is kind of what I refer to as a trophy wife feeling.
segments.textZh: 我有一种被贬到次要位置、被冷落的感觉，而且，你知道，这有点像我所说的那种花瓶妻子的感觉。

segments.textEn: Justine challenged a settlement offered by Musk in court and went public.
segments.textZh: 贾丝廷在法庭上对马斯克提出的和解方案发起挑战，并将事情公之于众。

segments.textEn: Justine takes her story to Marie Claire magazine, the Times of London newspaper and her own blog.
segments.textZh: 贾丝廷把她的故事讲给了《嘉人》杂志、英国《泰晤士报》，并写在了自己的博客上。

segments.textEn: On March 29, 2011, Justine announced that she was accepting a settlement for $10 million less than what Musk had offered before she took him to court.
segments.textZh: 2011年3月29日，贾丝廷宣布，她接受了一项和解方案，金额比马斯克在她将他告上法庭之前提出的金额少1000万美元。

segments.textEn: I got divorced. Personal life in somewhat of a shambles and in addition getting, you know, attacked by some in the media, my ex wife, every bad thing you could imagine.
segments.textZh: 我离婚了。个人生活有些一团糟，除此之外还受到，你知道，媒体中一些人的攻击，我的前妻，各种你能想象到的坏事。

segments.textEn: There were all kinds of crazy allegations around that, you know, allegations of affairs which have never been substantiated.
segments.textZh: 围绕这件事有各种疯狂的指控，你知道，还有从未得到证实的婚外情指控。

segments.textEn: Meanwhile, SpaceX, Musk's other company, hadn't been able to get a rocket into orbit.
segments.textZh: 与此同时，马斯克的另一家公司SpaceX一直没能将火箭送入轨道。

segments.textEn: He started saying, I've got enough money for three cracks at it. He put $100 million of his own money and he sort of hinted at the idea that after three, if he didn't make would be over, SpaceX would die.
segments.textZh: 他开始说，我的钱够尝试3次。他投入了自己的1亿美元，并且有点暗示说，3次之后，如果他没能成功，一切就结束了，SpaceX会死掉。

segments.textEn: The first launch didn't get very far. Got about a minute up and then there was an engine fire and that was it. The second flight actually did make it to space, but not to orbit. And then also Flight three, we didn't get all the way to orbit.

segments.textZh: 较量开始了。卢茨将亲自督导 Volt 的上市，这是一款全新的雪佛兰电动家庭轿车，旨在与 Tesla 的 Model S 竞争。马斯克的成功在 2010 年延续，他推动 Tesla 上市，并于 6 月宣布首次公开募股。但这一举动也让质疑 Tesla 的人大批涌现。

segments.textEn: Things really got ugly. I mean, they brought up the divorce, they brought up past problems at Tesla, they brought up, you know, Elon's background.
segments.textZh: 事情真的变得很难看。我的意思是，他们翻出了离婚的事，翻出了 Tesla 过去的问题，还翻出了，你知道，埃隆的背景。

segments.textEn: Tesla stock voted by Wall street as the least likely to succeed.
segments.textZh: Tesla 股票被华尔街评为最不可能成功的股票。

segments.textEn: You don't want to own this stock, you don't want to lease it.
segments.textZh: 你不会想持有这只股票，也不会想租赁它。

segments.textEn: Heck, you don't even.
segments.textZh: 见鬼，你甚至都不会。

segments.textEn: You shouldn't even rent the darn thing. We've confounded the critics at every turn. So at a certain point, people have to get tired of being wrong.
segments.textZh: 你甚至都不该租那该死的东西。我们在每一个转折点都让批评者大跌眼镜。所以到了一定时候，人们总该厌倦一错再错。

segments.textEn: There hasn't been an IPO of a car company in America since Henry Ford, and that caught people's attention.
segments.textZh: 自亨利·福特以来，美国还没有一家汽车公司进行过首次公开募股，而这引起了人们的注意。

segments.textEn: You just saw on his face this sort of just elation and this feeling like all of this suffering is worth it.
segments.textZh: 你能从他的脸上看到那种，就是那种欣喜若狂，还有一种感觉，仿佛所有这些苦难都是值得的。

segments.textEn: And it's.
segments.textZh: 而且它是。

segments.textEn: And we're.
segments.textZh: 而且我们。

segments.textEn: And it's real now.
segments.textZh: 而且它现在是真的了。

segments.textEn: The IPO was such a success that Tesla's net worth rose to almost $2 billion. And GM copied them again with an IPO of their own, the biggest in US history.
segments.textZh: 此次 IPO 大获成功，使 Tesla 的市值升至近20亿美元。通用汽车再次效仿，也进行了自己的 IPO，这是美国历史上规模最大的一次。

segments.textEn: Whether Tesla is ever hugely successful or not, I'll always owe him a debt of gratitude for having kind of broken the ice.
segments.textZh: 无论 Tesla 最终是否取得巨大成功，我都会永远感激他，因为他算是打破了坚冰。

segments.textEn: Around the same time, Daimler invested $50 million in Tesla, embarking on a joint venture to build electric Mercedes and smart cars.
segments.textZh: 大约在同一时期，戴姆勒向 Tesla 投资了5000万美元，启动了一项合资项目，以生产电动梅赛德斯和 smart 汽车。

segments.textEn: For a company like Daimler, the maker of Mercedes Benz, to suddenly award this contract to them, it was a validation.
segments.textZh: 像戴姆勒这样一家梅赛德斯-奔驰的制造商，突然把这份合同授予他们，这是一种认可。

segments.textEn: Toyota also invested $50 million to have Tesla build a new electric branch version of the RAV4.
segments.textZh: 丰田也投资了5000万美元，让 Tesla 制造新版 RAV4 电动分支车型。

segments.textEn: For a startup like Tesla, it's quite significant at this point. Tesla has received investment from the world's largest maker of luxury vehicles and the world's largest automaker.
segments.textZh: 对于 Tesla 这样的初创公司而言，这在现阶段意义相当重大。Tesla 已经获得了全球最大豪华汽车制造商和全球最大汽车制造商的投资。

segments.textEn: But Tesla still had an earnings problem. The company's loss for the fourth quarter of 2010 was $51.4 million, more than double the losses of the year before. That didn't stop Elon from taking one of his biggest risks ever, acquiring a huge car making plant near San Francisco, abandoned the previous year by Toyota.
segments.textZh: 但Tesla仍然存在盈利问题。该公司2010年第四季度亏损5140万美元，是前一年亏损额的2倍多。这并没有阻止埃隆去承担他有史以来最大的风险之一：收购旧金山附近的一座大型汽车制造工厂，这座工厂在前一年被丰田弃用。

segments.textEn: The dream factory location for Tesla was always the new ME factory, which was a 50% Toyota, 50% General Motors factory. It's one of the biggest car plants in the world. It's a great location, close to Tesla headquarters.
segments.textZh: Tesla梦想中的工厂地点一直是new ME工厂，那是一座丰田占50%、通用汽车占50%的工厂。它是世界上最大的汽车工厂之一。它的位置非常好，靠近Tesla总部。

segments.textEn: The reality is, for very little money, Toyota. Toyota got an albatross off its books. From an industry perspective, it looked incredibly savvy on Toyota's part and incredibly naive on Tesla's part. Car factories are big pieces of sunk capital. To retool a factory takes a tremendous incremental investment.
segments.textZh: 现实是，只花了很少的钱，丰田。丰田从账面上甩掉了一个沉重负担。从行业角度看，丰田显得极其精明，而Tesla则显得极其天真。汽车工厂是大笔的沉没资本。改造一座工厂需要巨额的增量投资。

segments.textEn: Musk took on critics of the electric car. In 2008, the BBC broadcast a review View of the Roadster by Top Gear's Jeremy Clarkson.
segments.textZh: 马斯克直面了电动汽车的批评者。2008年，BBC播出了《Top Gear》的杰里米·克拉克森对Roadster所作的评测看法。

segments.textEn: This car then really was shaping up to be something wonderful. But then, although Tesla say it'll do 200 miles, we worked out that on our track, it would run out after just 55 miles. And if it does run out, it's not a quick job to charge it up again.
segments.textZh: 这辆车当时确实逐渐展现出非凡之处。但随后，尽管Tesla说它能行驶200英里，我们算出它在我们的赛道上仅行驶55英里就会耗尽电量。而且如果电量真的耗尽，再次给它充满电并不是一件很快的事。

segments.textEn: Tesla charged that the incident was faked and said they had proof that the Roadster hadn't run out of power. In the spring of 2011, Tesla sued the BBC for libel and malicious falsehood to block reruns of the show. The case is now in court.
segments.textZh: Tesla指控该事件是伪造的，并表示他们有证据证明Roadster并未耗尽电量。2011年春季，Tesla以诽谤和恶意虚假陈述为由起诉BBC，以阻止该节目的重播。此案目前正在法院审理。

segments.textEn: But of all his companies, perhaps the greatest success could be the one addressing the world's energy needs. SolarCity continues to grow, now serving more than 10,000 customers from California to New York. It's the largest solar service provider in the US with more than 10,000 projects completed or underway.
segments.textZh: 但在他的所有公司中，或许最成功的会是那家致力于满足全球能源需求的公司。SolarCity持续发展，目前服务着从加利福尼亚州到纽约州的超过10,000名客户。它是美国最大的太阳能服务提供商，已完成或正在进行的项目超过10,000个。

segments.textEn: SolarCity has been very, very impressive. I mean, there are, you know, thousands of people with panels on their roofs and lots of big offices. I believe eBay has SolarCity panels. So it's having a very big, very visible impact on the world.
segments.textZh: SolarCity一直非常、非常令人印象深刻。我的意思是，有，你知道，数千人的屋顶上装有太阳能板，还有许多大型办公室。我相信eBay装有SolarCity的太阳能板。所以它正在对世界产生非常巨大、非常显眼的影响。

segments.textEn: He really wants to change the world. And in Elon Musk's vision of the future, you'll have clean and renewable sources of energy feeding the grid and all of our vehicles will run off that. This is really the future. It's something you want to tell stories about.
segments.textZh: 他真的想改变世界。而在埃隆·马斯克对未来的构想中，清洁、可再生的能源将输入电网，我们所有的车辆都将依靠这些能源运行。这确实是未来。这是你会想要讲述的故事。

segments.textEn: You know, he wants to do so many things. I mean, he has an idea for an electric jet, he wants to work on nuclear fusion. You know, he wants to remake the highways in Los Angeles.
segments.textZh: 你知道，他想做太多事情了。我的意思是，他有一个电动喷气式飞机的构想，他想研究核聚变。你知道，他想重建洛杉矶的高速公路。

segments.textEn: And in October 2010, Musk married Tallulah Riley.
segments.textZh: 2010年10月，马斯克与塔露拉·莱莉结婚。

segments.textEn: We spoke to them during their honeymoon in Paris.
segments.textZh: 他们在巴黎度蜜月期间，我们采访了他们。

segments.textEn: I feel incredibly blessed to be with the Elon for obviously so many reasons.
segments.textZh: 显然出于许许多多的原因，能和埃隆在一起，我感到无比幸运。

segments.textEn: As am I. Likewise.
segments.textZh: 我也是。同样。

segments.textEn: Thank you. Because I'm a visionary too. The past two years have been quite a ride, you know, and there's been some decisions that at the time I've been quaking in my boots over the things he's been doing. I feel privileged to be able to see them sort of so up close and witness it all.
segments.textZh: 谢谢。因为我也是个有远见的人。过去2年真是一段跌宕起伏的历程，你知道，有些决定，他当时做的那些事让我吓得双腿发抖。我觉得自己很荣幸，能够如此近距离地看到这些事，见证这一切。

segments.textEn: On December 8, 2010, SpaceX had its greatest mission yet.
segments.textZh: 2010年12月8日，SpaceX执行了迄今最伟大的任务。

segments.textEn: NASA just launched the SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket. The cargo vehicle is favored to replace the space shuttle when it retires next year.
segments.textZh: NASA刚刚发射了SpaceX的猎鹰9号火箭。这艘货运飞行器被看好在航天飞机明年退役后取而代之。

segments.textEn: For the first time in history, a commercial company's spacecraft was able to return from its orbit of the Earth and was recovered after a safe landing.
segments.textZh: 历史上首次，一家商业公司的航天器得以从环绕地球的轨道返回，并在安全着陆后被回收。

segments.textEn: Elon Musk goes a step further. Earth's not big enough with SpaceX. He literally wants to go to Mars and set up private colonies on moon Mars and push the vanguard of space exploration beyond that which governments are capable of doing, even superpowers. That is unprecedented.
segments.textZh: 埃隆·马斯克还要更进一步。对SpaceX来说，地球还不够大。他确实想前往火星，在月球、火星上建立私人殖民地，并把太空探索的前沿推进到政府甚至超级大国能力所不及之处。这是前所未有的。

segments.textEn: Elon has a self confidence that is just. It's breathtaking. And it's especially breathtaking when you think about the things he's confident about. The idea that humanity is going to get to Mars, that not just humanity is going to get to Mars, but that he, in his lifetime, Elon Musk will get to Mars.
segments.textZh: 埃隆有一种简直是。令人叹为观止的自信。而当你想到他所自信的那些事情时，就尤其令人叹为观止。他认为人类将抵达火星，不只是人类将抵达火星，而是他本人，埃隆·马斯克会在有生之年抵达火星。

segments.textEn: Musk and SpaceX are keeping the dream of man so space flight alive. In April 2011, the company announced that its Falcon Heavy rocket will be ready to launch in 2013. And on April 19, 2011, NASA confirmed its confidence in SpaceX by awarding them $75 million to develop a revolutionary launch escape system that one day would enable the Dragon spacecraft to carry astronauts safely to the moon and Mars.
segments.textZh: 马斯克和SpaceX让“人的所以太空飞行”这一梦想继续存在。2011年4月，该公司宣布其猎鹰重型火箭将于2013年准备好发射。2011年4月19日，NASA向其拨款7500万美元，用于开发一种革命性的发射逃逸系统，以此确认了其对SpaceX的信心；该系统有朝一日将使龙飞船能够把宇航员安全送往月球和火星。

segments.textEn: He finds a way to get from here to there with pragmatic steps. It's not just let's hunker down for 20 years, come up the other end with a dream and a vision. It's here's the incremental path of progress, here's how we can get from here to there.
segments.textZh: 他能找到一种通过务实步骤从这里走到那里的办法。这不只是让我们埋头苦干20年，最终带着梦想和愿景从另一端出来。而是，这里有一条循序渐进的发展路径，这就是我们如何从这里走到那里。

segments.textEn: Just is it significant, really? The question is, are things I'm working on, are they really going to matter or do they have the potential for really mattering?
segments.textZh: 只是，它真的重要吗？问题是，我正在做的事情，真的会有影响吗，或者它们是否有潜力真正产生影响？

segments.textEn: We don't know for sure if Elon Musk will revolutionize the world of automobiles with his electric car. We don't know if Musk will ever get to Mars or if he will really convert America to solar energy. We do know that Elon Musk will keep trying and there will be more innovative ideas along the way.
segments.textZh: 我们无法确定埃隆·马斯克是否会用他的电动汽车彻底改变汽车世界。我们不知道马斯克是否有朝一日会抵达火星，也不知道他是否真的会让美国转向太阳能。我们知道的是，埃隆·马斯克会继续尝试，一路上还会出现更多创新构想。

segments.textEn: Sam.
segments.textZh: 萨姆。
